blocks.text: Computer science mein maslon ko is base par solvable ya unsolvable kaha jata hai ke kya koi aisa algorithm maujood hai jo un ka hal de sake.

Solvable Problems (hal ho sakne wale masle): masla solvable hai agar koi algorithm use finite (khatam hone wale) waqt mein hal kar de. In maslon ke inputs aur outputs saaf hote hain aur hal tak pohanchne ka qadam ba qadam tareeqa maujood hota hai.

Misal: do integers ka greatest common divisor (GCD, yani sab se bara number jo dono ko poora divide kare) nikalna solvable masla hai. Euclidean algorithm GCD nikalne ka saaf aur finite tareeqa deta hai, is liye yeh solvable masle ki mashhoor misal hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Euclidean algorithm jore (a, b) ko (b, a ko b se divide karne ka remainder) se badalta rehta hai jab tak remainder 0 na ho jaye. GCD(48, 18): 48 = 2 x 18 + 12, 18 = 1 x 12 + 6, 12 = 2 x 6 + 0, to GCD = 6. Yeh misal hamari taraf se hai.
Yeh program Euclidean algorithm ke qadam print karta hai aur aakhir mein GCD batata hai. a aur b ki values badal kar Run karein; har dafa algorithm chand qadmon mein ruk jata hai (finite).

a = 48
b = 18

x, y = a, b
while y != 0:
    print(x, "=", x // y, "x", y, "+", x % y)
    x, y = y, x % y              # (a, b) becomes (b, remainder)
print("GCD of", a, "and", b, "is", x)

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"a = 48" aur "b = 18": woh do numbers jin ka GCD (sab se bara common divisor) chahiye.
"x, y = a, b": asal values kharab na hon is liye kaam x aur y par hota hai.
"while y != 0:": loop (baar baar chalne wala hissa) tab tak chalta hai jab tak remainder 0 na ho jaye.
"print(x, \"=\", x // y, \"x\", y, \"+\", x % y)": har qadam ki division likhta hai: // poora quotient (hissa) aur % remainder.
"x, y = y, x % y": Euclid ka asal qadam: (x, y) ki jagah (y, remainder) aa jata hai.
"print(\"GCD of\", ...)": loop khatam hone par x hi GCD hota hai.
Output: teen qadam "48 = 2 x 18 + 12", "18 = 1 x 12 + 6", "12 = 2 x 6 + 0", phir "GCD of 48 and 18 is 6".
Khud try karein: a = 100 aur b = 75 kar ke Run karein: do qadmon mein "GCD of 100 and 75 is 25" aayega.

Unsolvable Problems (hal na ho sakne wale masle): doosri taraf, masla unsolvable hai agar aisa koi algorithm banaya hi na ja sake jo har soorat (all cases) mein hal de. In maslon ka koi aam tareeqa nahi jo har mumkin input ke liye hal ki guarantee (pakka wada) de.

Misal: Halting Problem unsolvable masle ki mashhoor misal hai. Is mein yeh tay karna hota hai ke diya gaya program aakhir kar ruk jayega (halt, yani chalna khatam karega) ya hamesha chalta rahega. Alan Turing ne saabit kiya ke koi aam algorithm tamam mumkin program aur input ke joron ke liye Halting Problem hal nahi kar sakta; is liye yeh unsolvable masle ki basic misal hai.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Kisi mushkil masle par kaam shuru karne se pehle yeh tay karna zaroori hai ke masla solvable hai ya nahi. Is se waqt aur resources bachte hain, kyun ke aap aise masle par kaam karte hain jo algorithm se hal ho sakta hai.

blocks.prompt: Unsolvable problems ke baare mein kya sach hai (MCQ 3)?
blocks.explanation: (b) Unhein koi algorithm hal nahi kar sakta.

blocks.prompt: Halting Problem unsolvable kyun hai aur is ke implications (asar) kya hain, samjhaiye (long question 2).
blocks.explanation: Farz karein ek program H hamesha bata sakta hai ke koi program kisi input par rukega ya nahi. Ab aisa program D banayein jo H se khud D ke baare mein pooche aur phir ulta kare: H kahe 'D rukega' to D hamesha chalta rahe; H kahe 'D chalta rahega' to D ruk jaye. Is tarah H ka har jawab ghalat ho jata hai, to H maujood hi nahi ho sakta (Turing ka proof by contradiction: ulti baat maan kar dikhana ke woh ghalat hai). Implications (asar): koi tool har program ke na khatam hone wale loops nahi pakar sakta, programs ke kuch sawalon ka jawab kabhi automatic tareeqe se nahi mil sakta, aur computers ki kuch basic limits (hadein) hain.

items: Solvable: algorithm finite waqt mein hal de (48 aur 18 ka GCD = 6).
Unsolvable: koi algorithm tamam inputs par hal nahi de sakta (Halting Problem, Alan Turing).
